title: Trade, hold or leave it: choosing the defence
outcomes: Asks what the opponent threatens before choosing a defensive move
Counts the attackers before deciding that one exchange answers the attack
Chooses between a trade, a quiet hold and no defence at all, and rejects a trade that leaves a second attacker

steps.text: In **Trade off the piece doing the damage** you took away an attacker by exchanging. Now the harder question: is a trade the right answer at all? Under attack you can **trade** an attacker, **hold** by moving or guarding the target, or **counter-attack** with a bigger threat of your own. Start with the threat question: if I pass, what can he do? Then count his attackers.

**When a trade works.** It works when it removes an attacker he cannot replace. It fails when a second attacker is left: one exchange cannot answer two threats. **Rule of thumb:** count the attackers before you trade. A counter-attack is a third option only if your threat comes first and is bigger; no exercise here proves one.

steps.title: Same pieces, three answers
steps.prompt: White is to move in each position. Predict whether the best answer is a trade, a quiet hold by moving the queen, or no defence at all because nothing is threatened. Then check.

steps.text: No labels now. Some positions need a trade and some need another move. Ask the threat question first, then count attackers. The next four exercises are silent.

steps.prompt: Which step failed most often: asking what he threatens or counting the attackers? What will you do first next time?
